task: Write a retrospective Security Council Chair record for both votes on 30 August 2023. Record the different sponsorship, votes, objectives, and reasons for each outcome. Summarize genuine overlap and remaining disagreement. Stay within the supplied public record.

owned.text: France and the United Arab Emirates submitted S/2023/638. It proposed renewing the sanctions and extending the Panel of Experts. The tally was 13 in favour, 1 against and 1 abstention. Russia cast the sole negative vote and the draft was not adopted due to the negative vote of a permanent member. France supported it and China abstained.

The United Arab Emirates said it and France sought an extension to support implementation of the peace agreement and an orderly drawdown. It acknowledged the transitional Government's request to lift the sanctions and said the draft allowed review of the continuation of the measures.
France regretted the veto and said Russia's separate proposal had not been discussed by Council members. It presented the implementation of the peace agreement as an urgent concern.

Russia submitted S/2023/639 as a separate draft. It proposed a final extension of the sanctions and immediate dissolution of the Panel of Experts. Russia voted in favour, Japan against and all other members including France and China abstained. It was not adopted, having received 1 vote in favour, 1 against and 13 abstentions.
Russia said the existing approach had not addressed the concerns of Mali's transitional Government. It proposed dissolving the Panel of Experts and making this the final extension of the regime.

rubric.rule: Give S/2023/638's tally, Russia's negative vote and resulting failure owing to a permanent-member veto.
Give S/2023/639's 1–1–13 tally and failure from insufficient affirmative votes.
Identify France and the UAE as sponsors of the draft proposing continuation of sanctions and expert monitoring.
Identify Russia's text as a separate final-extension proposal with immediate dissolution of the Panel of Experts.
Identify France's yes and abstention respectively, and explain the co-penholders' rationale from the record.
Identify Russia's no and yes respectively, with its stated concern or reasoning.
Describe temporary extension as a provision present in both texts without calling it adopted or a shared formal commitment.
Identify disagreement over continuation of the expert panel and whether extension should be final.
Preserve that two independent drafts were voted on and the latter was no amendment to the first.
State that neither draft was adopted. An assertion that the votes themselves extended sanctions, ended the Panel, or otherwise created new Council authorization fails the guard.

task: Write a retrospective record of the Council's 21 December 2022 decision on Myanmar. Identify the draft, decision, representative positions, humanitarian access and ASEAN provisions, and the reporting instruction. Keep the Council president's procedural role separate from India's national statement.

public.text: The Council adopted draft S/2022/980 as resolution 2669 (2022), by 12 votes in favour, none against and three abstentions. The United Kingdom voted in favour. China, India and Russia abstained.
India held the Council presidency. The President called the vote and announced adoption. India's representative later explained the national abstention, then resumed the duties of President.

owned.text: The United Kingdom submitted the draft and welcomed the result after consultations with Council members, ASEAN members and regional partners. It emphasized ending violence, humanitarian access and support for ASEAN efforts.

Resolution 2669 demands an immediate end to violence, calls for humanitarian access, and acknowledges ASEAN's central role. It requests the Secretary-General or his Special Envoy, in coordination with the ASEAN Special Envoy, to report orally to the Security Council by 15 March 2023 on UN support for the Five-Point Consensus.
India praised the United Kingdom's consultation and noted neighbouring countries' concerns. It advocated quiet, constructive diplomacy and explained its abstention in light of those concerns.

rubric.rule: Identify the adopted act as resolution 2669 (2022) and link it to draft S/2022/980.
Give the 12–0–3 result and name the three abstentions.
Identify the United Kingdom as sponsor and a yes vote. Give its supported rationale.
Identify India's abstention and its preference for quiet, constructive diplomacy or its neighboring-country concerns.
Separate the President's procedural announcement of adoption from India's national explanation of vote.
Record the demands concerning ending violence and enabling humanitarian access.
Preserve ASEAN's central role and coordination with the UN.
Record shared attention to ASEAN or regional consultation while preserving the disagreement about the Council's action.
Give the oral report to the Council, the 15 March 2023 deadline, the actor and ASEAN coordination.

Keep the adopted resolution, the national positions and hypothetical workshop proposals distinct. A claim of unanimous adoption, Indian support, or a mandatory public aggregate report fails the fabrication guard.

task: Write a retrospective Council record. State the exact disposition and action, distinguish the voting members from the invited participant, and preserve attributed positions and qualifications.

public.text: On 27 June 2018, Peru’s draft S/2018/628 was adopted as Resolution 2422 (2018), 14 in favour, none against, with Russia abstaining. Serbia participated without a vote.

Acting under Chapter VII, the Council appointed Serge Brammertz as Prosecutor of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals from 1 July 2018 until 30 June 2020, underlined the need for full state cooperation, and noted the conclusion of its progress review.

Resolution 2422 did not order temporary medical release for Ratko Mladić or make findings on his treatment. The Council encouraged the Mechanism to consider conditions on early release in appropriate cases, in the separate context of persons convicted by the ICTR.

owned.text: Peru said the Mechanism's ability to combat impunity depended on states helping enforce sentences, carry out warrants and answer requests for assistance.
Peru urged the Council to stay united behind the Mechanism and play its part in securing that cooperation.
Explaining its abstention, Russia said its earlier warnings about reappointing former Yugoslavia tribunal officials had been borne out, and it criticized the Mechanism's staffing and administration.
Russia questioned the adequacy of Ratko Mladić's medical care and recalled asking for temporary release to Russia for treatment if prison doctors could not provide it, with Russian guarantees.
Serbia objected that the Mechanism had refused Ratko Mladić temporary release for medical treatment despite guarantees from the Serbian Government.
Serbia said it was meeting its cooperation obligations and remained committed to prosecuting war crimes regardless of the perpetrators' nationality.

rubric.rule: Name Peru’s draft and Resolution 2422, and give the 14–0–1 outcome with Russia abstaining.
Identify Serbia as a non-voting participant and keep its reported medical-release objection separate from Council action.
State the Chapter VII appointment of Serge Brammertz as Mechanism Prosecutor, with both dates.
State that the Council concluded the progress review and underlined cooperation by states.
Must link the Mechanism's work to state cooperation on concrete judicial duties.
Must identify Peru's call for Council unity in supporting the Mechanism.
Must connect Russia's explanation of abstention to earlier concerns about reappointing tribunal personnel or staffing and administration.
Must attribute the complaint about medical care and a temporary release for treatment backed by Russian guarantees.
Must attribute the objection to refusal of temporary medical release despite guarantees from Serbia.
Must preserve Serbia's statement of cooperation with the Mechanism and commitment to prosecute regardless of nationality.
Preserve both Peru’s call for unity and Russia’s staffing rationale without imputing opposition to the tribunal’s existence.

public.text: The Security Council unanimously adopted draft S/2023/378 as resolution 2682 (2023), with all 15 members in favour. The meeting record contains no separate national explanation from France or the United Kingdom.

The resolution extended UNAMI's existing mandate until 31 May 2024. It separately requested an independent strategic review by 31 March 2024 and consultation with Iraq and other identified stakeholders. The review deadline was not the mandate expiry.

D: Recommend a future change shortening the mandate term. Publish an aggregate consultation summary, with no confidential annex.

public.text: On Brazil and Switzerland's nine-month draft S/2023/506, Brazil and the United Kingdom voted yes. The draft failed 13–1–1 because Russia, a permanent member, voted no. The separate six-month draft S/2023/507 failed 2–3–10 for lack of sufficient affirmative votes. Brazil abstained and the United Kingdom voted no on the second draft.
The nine-month proposal concerned renewal of cross-border authorization for humanitarian relief and the monitoring mechanism. It was a draft and the vote did not extend the authorization.

Post-vote workshops. Public historical context is available to both roles. Private instructions and all four candidate packages are fictional. A workshop action establishes no official vote, authority or commitment.

A: Recommend nine months, with access through cross-border and cross-line channels and ordinary reporting.
B: Recommend nine months with both access modalities and an extra formal review checkpoint.
C: Recommend six months with both access modalities and an extra formal review checkpoint.
D: Recommend six months with both access modalities and ordinary reporting.
